Origin: reflect light from #2785

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:docs-health` filed #2785 proposing specific replacement text for a dangling
commit-hash citation ("squashed into `15553cf`", "`41dc8424f` is not a resolvable object in
this repository"). #2785's own build phase, running a full (unshallowed) history fetch, found
both claims in the *proposed replacement* itself were wrong: `41dc8424f` is a real commit
(just unreachable from `main`), and `15553cf` never touches the files in question — the
actual landing commit is `cdb32b046`. The record had to be fixed against its own proposed fix
text, not just its originally-flagged problem.

## Deliverables

`docs-health`'s staleness-finding procedure for a dangling-commit-hash finding should run (or
instruct the filing pass to run) a full/unshallowed `git log`/`git branch -r --contains` check
against the proposed replacement commit hash(es) before filing — the same check #2785's build
phase had to redo independently — so a filed record's "Proposed" text is not itself stale on
arrival.

## Acceptance Criteria

A dangling-commit-hash staleness finding `docs-health` files includes a replacement citation
that has already been verified reachable (or explicitly marked unresolvable) against full
repo history, not just the shallow-clone view available at filing time.

---

**Doc:** docs/releasing.md | **Id:** releasing | **Section:** After the merge: which release carried it | **Category:** staleness | **Misleads:** coding agent | **Classification:** additive | **Confidence:** med

Verified-as-of: 9e7cee5dc92cfe8e4b7a431f1ad6aead907e2250

## Current State

docs/releasing.md says 'Unchanged — `_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md` Step 4.1 answers this from tag ancestry alone' and then shows only `git describe --tags --contains --first-parent --match 'v*' <merge-sha>`. The canonical source it cites (plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md lines 24-27) shows `git fetch origin {integration-branch}` immediately before that same `git describe` line, and explicitly explains why: 'Read it after the merge is confirmed and after the fetch above — a sibling session's tag can land while this PR is being merged.' That race is not hypothetical — the same file cites #603/#678 as the incident that motivated this step. A reader (especially an agent doing a literal copy-paste rather than following the cross-reference) who runs docs/releasing.md's snippet as shown risks a stale/incorrect 'not yet in a release' verdict if a sibling session's tag landed moments earlier and was never fetched locally.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
````
```
git describe --tags --contains --first-parent --match 'v*' <merge-sha>
```
````

**Proposed:**
````
```
git fetch origin <integration-branch>
git describe --tags --contains --first-parent --match 'v*' <merge-sha>
```
````

## Acceptance Criteria

The code block under 'After the merge: which release carried it' in docs/releasing.md includes `git fetch origin <integration-branch>` before the `git describe` command, matching the full command sequence in `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md` Step 4.1, which the doc claims to mirror unchanged.

## Release Note

No user-visible change — documentation accuracy fix.

_Filed by `/claude-tweaks:docs-health`. Close to resolve; label `wontfix` to suppress future reports of this finding._

Origin: reflect full (multi-spec batch) from #2633/#2664

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

At the start of run 2026-09-30T190052-spec-2633-2664, `flow-preflight` classified the freshly minted run dir as adoption **case 3** (an adopted, already-running run), not case 2 (a fresh mint).

The cause was the issue-claim step, which had already appended its claim-log lines to `decisions.md`. The preflight treated a non-empty `decisions.md` as evidence of a prior run. The executor ruled case 2 by hand and logged the ruling.

A case-3 misclassification would have triggered the case-3 adoption-recovery backfill (`flow/steps-and-gates.md`) on a run that had nothing to recover.

## Deliverables

1. The preflight's case classification ignores `decisions.md` entries written by the claim step, recognized by their claim-log section or line shape, when deciding fresh vs adopted.
2. Add a regression test with a run dir whose `decisions.md` holds only claim-log lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A run dir with only claim-log lines in `decisions.md` classifies as case 2.
- A run dir with any non-claim decision entry still classifies as it does today.

## Release Note

Freshly started /flow runs are no longer mistaken for resumed ones after claiming their records.

## Current State

`_shared/pr-run-comments.md` finds and updates each run-comment kind by a first-line marker (`<!-- run-comment: verdict -->`), one comment per kind per PR. A `/flow` multi-spec run shares one PR across N specs, and each spec's `/review` Step 7 posts a verdict. The documented find-and-update would make spec N's verdict silently overwrite specs 1..N-1's, and the file has no multi-spec rule.

Run 2026-09-30T190052-spec-2633-2664 ruled ad hoc: it kept one cumulative comment with a per-spec section that each spec's review updates in place (`decisions.md`, spec-2633 Step 7).

## Deliverables

1. `_shared/pr-run-comments.md` states the multi-spec rule: one cumulative `verdict` comment per shared PR, with one `### #{n}` section per spec, and each spec's review replacing only its own section.
2. `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 7 cites it.
3. Add a conformance test pinning the rule's presence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pr-run-comments.md` names the multi-spec cumulative-section rule, and Step 7 cites it.
- A conformance test fails when the rule text is removed.

## Release Note

Multi-spec pipeline runs keep every spec's review verdict on the shared PR instead of the last one overwriting the rest.

Origin: reflect hindsight from #2664

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Four readers each carry their own copy of the multi-spec "per-spec run dir falls back to its parent for the shared worktree/PR stamps" rule:

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` `resolveState` (#1930 review C1) — fills `worktree`/`pr` from the parent.
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` `resolvePrNumber` — reads the parent `run-state.json` when the per-spec one is absent (a different rule: whole-file fallback, not per-field).
- `plugin/bin/lib/pr-bookkeeping/precondition.js` `checkPrBookkeepingPrecondition` (#2664) — per-field fill of `worktree`/`pr`/`prExempt` plus the parent `decisions.md` degrade line.
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md:88` — prose: reads `pr` on the parent `run-state.json`.

The three code copies already disagree on semantics (per-field fill vs whole-file fallback; `/^spec-/` basename gate in two, none in `resolvePrNumber`; `prExempt` honored in one). A fifth reader will copy whichever it finds first.

## Deliverables

1. One exported helper beside `readRunState` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` (e.g. `readRunStateWithParent(runDir)`) implementing the per-field fill for `worktree`/`pr`/`prExempt` behind the `/^spec-/` basename gate, returning `{ state, parentRunDir }`.
2. Migrate `pack.js` `resolveState`, `engine-verify.js` `resolvePrNumber`, and `precondition.js` to it; keep each call site's existing tests green.
3. `resolvePrNumber`'s whole-file fallback converges on the per-field rule (a per-spec `run-state.json` carrying only `status` must still find the parent PR) — add a test for that shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `grep -rn "path.dirname(runDir), 'run-state.json'" plugin/bin` returns no hits outside the new helper.
- A per-spec dir with a status-only `run-state.json` resolves the parent PR in all three consumers (one test each).
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

No user-visible change — internal consolidation of how multi-spec pipeline runs locate their shared worktree and PR.

## Current State

Three /specify sub-files sit within a few hundred bytes of the 28,672-byte per-sub-file ceiling that `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` pins (`SPECIFY_SUBFILE_CEILING_BYTES = 28 * 1024`): `spec-template.md` 28,666 B, `shaping-mode-stamping.md` 28,523 B, `next-mode.md` 28,454 B (measured at b3c936252).

Two gaps from #2827 need room in `shaping-mode-stamping.md` that it no longer has: shaping mode's born-ready "already shaped, no-op" classification (`shaping-mode.md`, and the stamping file's Actions Performed rows) is judged by eye rather than by `compose-record.js --check` exiting 0; and the local-files driver's pre-write `--check` exists only in prose, with no conformance test (the github-issues fence has one in `tests/specify-shaping-template-required-sections.test.js`).

## Deliverables

1. Split the three near-ceiling /specify sub-files along their existing section boundaries into lazy-loaded siblings, each well under the ceiling, and repoint every citation (SKILL.md routing, `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table, tests that read them by path).

2. Make shaping mode's "already shaped, no-op" classification the result of `compose-record.js --check` exiting 0 on the live body, not a by-eye judgment.

3. Add a conformance test pinning the local-files driver's pre-write `--check` line, matching the github-issues fence's existing test.

- [ ] A body that `compose-record.js --check` accepts is reported "already shaped, no-op" and a body it rejects never is — asserted by a test.

Origin: ledger resolve gate (#2827/#2828 run, ledger item 1)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

`tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml` pins `impeccable-plugin` at 4.0.2, and `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/impeccable-plugin.md` carries the matching `<!-- upstream-pin: impeccable-plugin@4.0.2 -->`. The maintainer machine's plugin cache holds 3.0.6, 4.2.2, 4.3.1 and 4.4.0 (enabled at user scope: 4.4.0) and no 4.0.2, so `checkVersion` reports `breach` and three tests in `tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js` fail on every local `npm test`: "the installed plugin matches the pinned version", "gatherSignals() executes cleanly and returns the documented shape" and "the CLI entrypoint accepts no flags". CI has no Impeccable install, so the same tests skip there as `absent`.

Every local run since the pin fell behind reports these 3 failures, which each pipeline run has to re-diagnose as environmental (the #2827/#2828 run logged them as its ledger item 1). Related: #2531 provisions sandbox plugin caches at whatever the pin is; this record moves the pin itself forward to the version maintainers run, so the two are complementary.

## Deliverables

1. Re-pin `impeccable-plugin` to the version installed at user scope (4.4.0 at filing time — re-check with `claude plugin list`) in `tools/upstream-drift/manifest.yml` and `impeccable-plugin.md`'s pin comment together.

2. Re-verify every `assertions` entry for `impeccable-plugin` in the manifest against that version's `skills/impeccable/scripts/context-signals.mjs`, and update `impeccable-plugin.md`'s claims where upstream changed.

3. Re-record `tests/fixtures/impeccable-plugin/` against the new version, per its README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js` passes with no failures on a machine whose enabled Impeccable is the new pin.
- [ ] `node tools/upstream-drift/run.js` reports `ok` for `impeccable-plugin`.
- [ ] The manifest pin and `impeccable-plugin.md`'s pin comment name the same version (the existing pin-parity test passes).

## Release Note

No user-visible change: updated the pinned Impeccable plugin version the design-wrapper contract tests check against.

Origin: consolidated Review Console — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`, ledger row #20 (residual scope; the reflect finding's plan-level half was already applied as a skill update at `301a7351b`)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Adding a flag to a skill requires updating every *syntactic mirror* of that skill's argument surface.
The count of those mirrors is currently carried in a plan author's head, and it has been wrong twice:

- **#679** established "a new flag has exactly two syntactic-mirror surfaces beyond the Input table"
  — the `argument-hint` frontmatter line and the Input parse line.
- **#2759** proved that convention was itself an undercount. Task 3 updated both named surfaces;
  Task 6's full-suite gate then found a **third**: `plugin/skills/help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes`
  column, byte-pinned by `tests/reference-card-argument-hint.test.js` under #564. Fixed at `613e230`.

It was caught only by luck of two coincidences: that a byte-pinning suite happened to exist for that
particular surface, and that the run's gate compared failing-file **sets** per file rather than
totals (346 failures against a 395 baseline reads as an improvement; only the per-file diff exposed
the new red file).

The plan-authoring half of the fix has shipped: `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` now
carries "Derive a flag's mirror surfaces by grepping for an existing flag rather than from a
remembered count" (applied this run at `301a7351b`). That makes the next plan author less likely to
undercount. It does **not** make the enumeration canonical, and it does not make an undercount
detectable — which is the residual this record covers.

## Deliverables

- One canonical enumeration of every `argument-hint` mirror surface — a named table in
  `docs/skill-authoring.md`, or a new `plugin/skills/_shared/argument-hint-mirrors.md` — listing the
  frontmatter line, the Input parse line, and `help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes` column as permanent
  entries, with room for the next one.
- One conformance test that walks that enumeration **mechanically** for every skill, so a skill whose
  flag set disagrees across surfaces fails by construction rather than by whichever byte-pin happens
  to exist.
- Retire the "exactly two surfaces" wording wherever it still appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

Adding a flag to any skill's `argument-hint` and leaving `help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes` column
stale fails the new conformance test — proven by making that exact change and showing the test red,
then green after the mirror is updated.

The enumeration lives in exactly one file; no other file restates the list (this repo's
Cross-references convention).

Every existing skill passes the new test at the time it lands, or the exceptions are named.

_Filed by the consolidated Review Console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`), from
`spec-2759/staged/reflect-1.md`._

## Release Note

Made the list of places a skill's argument hint must match canonical and checked automatically.

Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: blocked-dependency

## Current State

`wrap-up/review-console.md`'s Multi-spec defer protocol step 4 instructs writing `{run-dir}/verify-expectations.json` (`{"version":1,"memory":[],"upstream":[],"deferred":[...]}`) into the pipeline run directory. The three sanctioned run-dir writers documented in `gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md` — `log-decision.js` (`decisions.md`), `stage-item.js` (`staged/`), `set-config.js` (`config.yml`) — cover exactly three filenames; none covers this one. A direct `Write` to the main-checkout run-dir path from a worktree-isolated per-spec session is refused by the PreToolUse worktree-isolation gate.

Observed twice in the same multi-spec run (2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759): `spec-2758`'s wrap-up hit this gap and logged it as ledger #19 of `docs/plans/2026-09-21-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759-ledger.md`, flagging it for "the run's final wrap-up, which can write it once outside worktree isolation, or a backlog record proposing a fourth sanctioned writer CLI for this file class." `spec-2759`'s wrap-up (the run's actual final spec) re-confirmed the same gap still applies — it is also still a worktree-isolated session, so it cannot write the file either. The bounded consequence (per `review-console.md`): a per-spec `verify` run renders `memory-updates`/`upstream-feedback` as `unknown (expectations file missing)` instead of `skip (nothing recorded)` — accepted, does not block the consolidated Review Console, which reads `decisions.md`/`staged/` directly.

## Deliverables

A fourth sanctioned run-dir writer CLI (or an added mode on an existing one) covering `verify-expectations.json`, following the same `run(argv, deps)` seam, exit-code vocabulary, and run-dir anchoring guard as `log-decision.js`/`stage-item.js`/`set-config.js` (`gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI wrapper contract).

## Acceptance Criteria

A worktree-isolated `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` session can write `spec-{n}/verify-expectations.json` (or update it) via the new/extended sanctioned CLI without tripping the PreToolUse worktree-isolation gate — verified by a regression test exercising the CLI from a simulated worktree-isolated context.

`review-console.md`'s per-spec `verify` step no longer needs the `unknown (expectations file missing)` fallback once the file is actually written — the memory-updates/upstream-feedback probe reads `skip (nothing recorded)` normally.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._

## Release Note

Added a sanctioned way to record verification expectations from a worktree-isolated wrap-up.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`design-wrapper` currently routes design-quality work to Impeccable only. A described set of five Claude Code design plugins includes a Taste skill (anti-slop styling, 76k GitHub stars) and a Web Design Guidelines skill (audits against Vercel's rules including accessibility).

## Deliverables

- Trial the Taste and Web Design Guidelines skills against a sample build alongside Impeccable's own passes.
- Decide whether either complements or duplicates Impeccable's finish-reviewer/asset-producer roles.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A short comparison note on overlap/gaps versus Impeccable, checked into `design-wrapper`'s docs.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: evaluated the Taste and Web Design Guidelines skills for design reviews.

## Technical Approach

Run Taste and Web Design Guidelines against the same sample build `design-wrapper`'s Impeccable passes (`impeccable-finish-reviewer`, `impeccable-asset-producer`) already cover, and compare findings directly: does either surface issues Impeccable misses (e.g. Web Design Guidelines' accessibility rules against Vercel's own bar), or does either largely duplicate Impeccable's existing critique? Write the comparison as a short note, landing in `design-wrapper`'s docs alongside its existing mode documentation.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/` — the existing Impeccable-routed passes to compare against
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/` docs — where the comparison note lands

## Gotchas

- Both third-party skills are external plugins this repo doesn't own — availability/version drift should be noted in the comparison if either isn't stably installable.
- This is a comparison-and-decide record — a "duplicates Impeccable, no action" outcome is a valid, complete result, not a failure to find value.

## Original request

Evaluate Taste/Web-Design-Guidelines skills for design-wrapper

Current State:
- design-wrapper currently routes design-quality work to Impeccable only.
- A reel names five Claude Code design plugins: a Taste skill (anti-slop styling, 76k GitHub stars), a Web Design Guidelines skill (audits against Vercel's rules incl. accessibility), a full design-system skill, 21st Dev MCP (10k+ UI components), and Playwright CLI for self-screenshot review.

Deliverables:
- Trial the Taste and Web Design Guidelines skills against a sample build alongside Impeccable's own passes.
- Decide whether either complements or duplicates Impeccable's finish-reviewer/asset-producer roles.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A short comparison note on overlap/gaps versus Impeccable, checked into design-wrapper's docs.

Surface: backend

## Current State

Record #649 added `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s fan-out single-assistant-message-rule
sentence and per-site citations (AC1, fully test-pinned in `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`,
18/18 passing). AC2 — "A `/specify` red-team over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues launches its
personas in ≤ (number of sub-issues) assistant messages, verified in the transcript by `Agent`
tool_use blocks sharing a message id" — is a live-behavior criterion that cannot be verified by a
static `node --test` assertion; it can only be confirmed by observing an actual future `/specify`
decomposition run's transcript.

## Deliverables

Confirm, at the next `/specify` decomposition run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues, that
persona dispatch actually batches into ≤N assistant messages per `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
fan-out single-assistant-message rule and `red-team.md`'s per-sub-issue batching unit. Record the
observation (transcript excerpt or note) against this item, or file a defect against
`red-team.md`'s dispatch prose if it does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

A `/specify` run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues is observed; its persona `Agent` tool_use
calls are confirmed (via transcript `tool_use` block message-id grouping) to arrive in ≤ (number of
sub-issues) assistant messages.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: verified that spec red-team reviews batch correctly across several sub-issues.

## Technical Approach

Wait for (or trigger) a `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposition-mode run that produces 2 or more
`ceremony:standard` sub-issue records — `ceremony-check` (`assess-agent-autonomy/ceremony-check.md`)
resolves the tier per sub-issue during that run's own Step 3, so the tier isn't knowable until the
run happens. Once such a run occurs, inspect that session's stored transcript for the Step 5
red-team dispatch (`specify/red-team.md`'s Parallel dispatch section): locate the `Agent` tool_use
blocks for each dispatched persona and group them by the assistant message id each block belongs
to. Confirm the number of distinct assistant message ids covering all persona dispatches for a
given sub-issue is ≤ the number of sub-issues in that batch. Use the same read-only transcript
inspection method `transcript-payload-verification` documents for reading this session's own
locally-stored transcript, rather than instrumenting or modifying `red-team.md` itself.

If the count exceeds the bound, file a defect issue against `red-team.md`'s dispatch prose
(quoting the transcript grouping that violates the rule) instead of editing the file directly from
this record — this record's own deliverable is the observation, not the fix.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/specify/red-team.md` — the per-sub-issue persona dispatch procedure being observed
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the fan-out single-assistant-message rule this observation verifies compliance with
- `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — AC1's existing static test coverage (unaffected by this record)

## Gotchas

- This record's acceptance criterion depends on an external event (a live `/specify` decomposition
  run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues happening) that this record cannot itself trigger on a
  fixed schedule — it may sit open for some time until a qualifying run occurs naturally, or until
  someone deliberately runs one to close it out.
- A qualifying run must be observed via its own transcript at the time it happens; this record
  cannot be resolved from historical data if no already-completed run's transcript is still
  available.

Verify /specify red-team fan-out batching at next live multi-sub-issue run (#649 AC2)

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2744, #2748 (same shape — pure verification-and-close findings, already-resolved by the time of shaping)

## Current State

This is a dispatch-filed self-report from a `/flow` Step 2.8 claim contest: a dispatch firing (run `2026-09-21T102115-record-1982`) re-selected a file-overlap group (`#2568, #2565, #2346, #2330, #1982`) that was already claimed by an earlier run (`2026-09-21T002427-record-1982`), found the claim contested (stale-looking, TTL expiring `2026-09-24`), claimed nothing (all-or-abort), and stopped before Step 3 — a clean, correct no-op per `flow/claim-targets.md`'s own procedure. The report recommended `/claude-tweaks:tidy` to sweep and reclaim, or waiting for the TTL to expire.

**Verified during shaping — this is now fully resolved, not a live issue.** The claims-registry blob for `#1982` (`gh api repos/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/contents/claims/issue-1982.json?ref=claims-registry`) shows `{"released": true, "runId": "2026-09-21T002427-record-1982", "reason": "issue-closed: reconciled from #1982", "releasedAt": "2026-09-23T18:37:15.498Z"}` — the claim was properly released via reconciliation nearly a week before this shaping pass. `#1982` itself is `CLOSED` (confirmed via `gh issue view 1982 --json state`). The TTL this report flagged (`2026-09-24`) has also long since passed. There is no remaining stale claim, no group to reclaim, and no code defect to fix — this record's entire purpose (surface a contested claim for a human/tidy to resolve) has already been served by the ordinary reconciliation machinery, independent of this record.

## Deliverables

- Confirm the claim/contest state is still resolved at build time (re-check the claims-registry blob and `#1982`'s state — this shaping pass's snapshot could theoretically be stale if something re-contested the same group, though nothing suggests that).
- Close this self-report with a comment citing the resolution evidence (the released claim blob, `#1982`'s closed state) — no code change, no reclaim action needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh check confirms the claim is released and `#1982` is closed (or reports a genuine surprise if not, rather than assuming this shaping pass's finding still holds).
- The record is closed with an explanatory comment, not left open as if still actionable.
- `npm test` passes (no test-affecting change expected).

## Release Note

No user-visible change: closed out a resolved claim contest reported by a headless dispatch.

## Technical Approach

Pure verification-and-close — the same shape as #2744's already-resolved finding. No code investigation needed beyond re-confirming the claims-registry state via `gh api` and the target issue's state via `gh issue view`.

### Key Files

- None — no code change. The claims-registry blob (`claims/issue-1982.json` on the `claims-registry` branch) and issue `#1982`'s state are the only things to re-verify.

## Gotchas

- Don't mistake this for a genuine unresolved claim-contest needing a `/tidy` reclaim sweep — the evidence gathered during shaping shows it was already reconciled independently, five to six days before this shaping pass ran.
- If re-verification at build time contradicts this (the claim shows live again, or `#1982` is reopened), stop and report that explicitly — it would mean something unusual happened since this shaping pass, worth surfacing rather than silently re-closing.

## Original request

Dispatch headless self-report: flow-step-2.8-claim-contest

## Flow: Claim contested

#2568, #2565, #2346, #2330, #1982 (this dispatch bundle, file-overlap group keyed to record 1982)
are already claimed by run 2026-09-21T002427-record-1982 (session
1522dc69-eb55-5ecb-8312-e2ac906cf0c4, host: vm, claimed 2026-09-21T00:32:49.141Z, expires
2026-09-24T00:32:49.141Z).

Stale holder — no activity since unknown (no transcript found at
~/.claude/projects/-home-user-claude-tweaks/1522dc69-eb55-5ecb-8312-e2ac906cf0c4.jsonl or
~/.claude/projects/-home-user-claude-tweaks--claude-worktrees-dispatch-next/1522dc69-eb55-5ecb-8312-e2ac906cf0c4.jsonl;
same host (vm) as this firing, so not a Remote holder; no git worktree in this checkout's
`git worktree list` matches the holder's bare `record-1982` runId token, so no in-progress worktree
was found to inspect). Next: `/claude-tweaks:tidy` to sweep and reclaim, or wait for the TTL to
expire.

This dispatch firing (run 2026-09-21T102115-record-1982, PIPELINE_RUN_DIR
/home/user/claude-tweaks/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-21T102115-record-1982) re-selected the
same file-overlap group ~10 hours after the still-live claim above was written, never claimed any
of the 5 targets itself (all-or-abort: the first target checked was already contested, so nothing
was claimed and nothing needs releasing), and stopped before Step 3 (Config Manifesto) per
`flow/claim-targets.md`'s group-claim-all-or-abort procedure. No build or test ran for this
firing.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2799 (trim skill descriptions per newer-model guidance) — the more directly actionable lever for the same underlying concern (skill-listing context cost), since a plugin controls its own skill descriptions but not Claude Code's own skill-listing mechanism (see Current State).

## Current State

Claude Code lists every installed skill every session, capped at 1% of context — this is platform (harness) behavior, not something a plugin like claude-tweaks controls directly. `jev-skill-suggestion` reportedly gates that listing behind a fast classifier instead, but that would require either a harness-level feature claude-tweaks can't implement itself, or a wrapper/orchestration layer outside the plugin's own scope. What claude-tweaks *can* actually influence is the size and count of its own installed skills' descriptions — the same lever #2799 already targets.

## Deliverables

Investigate what a plugin actually has leverage over here, given Claude Code's skill-listing mechanism is platform behavior:
1. Confirm whether any plugin-level mechanism exists (today, or documented as planned) to conditionally register/hide skills from the per-session listing — if one exists, evaluate whether claude-tweaks' skill count/structure would benefit from using it.
2. If no such mechanism exists, determine whether the more direct lever — reducing description size/count (#2799's scope) and consolidating near-duplicate or rarely-triggered skills — is the actual available answer, and state that explicitly rather than pursuing an unavailable "gate" mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A concrete answer is recorded to "does Claude Code expose any plugin-level skill-listing gate today" — not assumed either way.
- If no such mechanism exists, this record's outcome explicitly redirects to #2799's already-shaped scope (description trimming) rather than treating the gate idea as still open, so the investigation lands somewhere actionable instead of dead-ending.
- If a mechanism does exist, a follow-up evaluation of whether claude-tweaks' current skill set would benefit is at least scoped (even if not fully executed in this same record).

## Release Note

No user-visible change: evaluated whether the plugin can gate which skills load per project.

## Technical Approach

Research Claude Code's actual documented plugin/skill-loading behavior first — whether any conditional-registration or lazy-listing mechanism is exposed to plugins today. This determines which of the two Deliverable branches applies; the record intentionally doesn't presuppose which.

### Key Files

- None specific to claude-tweaks' own codebase — this is primarily a platform-capability investigation; any resulting action likely lands in #2799's scope (skill description trimming) rather than new code here

## Gotchas

- Don't build a custom skill-gating mechanism inside claude-tweaks itself as a workaround if the platform doesn't expose one — that would be reimplementing harness-level behavior at the plugin layer, a much larger and riskier undertaking than this capture's one-line scope suggests, and almost certainly not what was intended.
- This record's most likely real outcome is "the answer is #2799" — don't treat that as a non-finding; explicitly stating that redirect is itself the useful conclusion.

## Original request

Evaluate a jev-skill-suggestion-style skill-loading gate

Context: Claude Code lists every installed skill every session, capped at 1% of context; jev-skill-suggestion gates that behind a fast classifier instead.

Scope: Whether claude-tweaks' own skills could be gated similarly to save context.

groups.body:
## Current State

`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` documents that `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 1.6 ("Remote-only stale branch check") exists specifically so a same-name branch left on `origin` by a prior, unrelated run is caught and stopped for a decision *before* `EnterWorktree` creates the new worktree and before Step 2's push can be rejected non-fast-forward. On run `2026-09-30T102540-record-2625` (#2625, dispatch group, worktree branch `worktree-dispatch-next`), the first (`build,test`) call's own `decisions.md` entry records that Step 2's push nonetheless failed non-fast-forward twice, against a genuinely unrelated stale branch left by a different old run (commit `c19a97b7a`, re #2266, ~61 commits behind current main) — exactly the shape Step 1.6 is supposed to close. The run proceeded local-only with `prExempt: true` stamped in `run-state.json` rather than stopping for the documented decision, and the second call had to resolve it manually (rename + push to a disambiguated branch name).

## Deliverables

Investigate why Step 1.6's remote-only stale-branch check did not fire (or fired but did not stop the run) for this collision — confirm whether it ran at all, and if it did, why its outcome didn't prevent the subsequent non-fast-forward push. Fix the gap so a genuinely unrelated same-name remote branch is caught before worktree creation, consistent with the documented contract, rather than surfacing only as a failed push two steps later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reproduction (or an audit of Step 1.6's actual invocation site) identifies why the check did not stop this run.
2. Step 1.6 (or its invocation) is fixed so an unrelated same-name remote branch is caught pre-emptively for a `pr-first` dispatch-orchestrated worktree run, not just handled reactively after a failed push.
3. No regression to the legitimate resume case (a same-name branch that IS this run's own prior attempt) — Step 1.6 must still distinguish "mine" from "someone else's stale leftover."

## Release Note

Internal maintenance — no user-visible change.

## Suggested resolution

Start by reading `build/worktree-setup.md` Step 1.6 and confirming it was actually invoked in this run's first call (check for a `decisions.md` line at that step) — the observed evidence stops at "push failed twice," short of enough context to state a root cause with confidence.

Origin: reflect full mode from #2625's wrap-up. Defer-reason: tangential.
